report:
### Sample adequacy
20 fields analysed, 20 white cells counted. All fields contained white cells. Red cells 152 (~7.6/field), platelets 16 (~0.8/field). Red cell count is indicative (undercount on crowded fields). 3 uncertain detections were kept only because fields had no sure white cell – they may not be white cells at all. With fewer than 100 white cells the differential is only indicative.

### Differential – indicative (20 white cells)
Counts: neutrophil 7 (35.0%), lymphocyte 4 (20.0%), monocyte 2 (10.0%), eosinophil 1 (5.0%), basophil 1 (5.0%), ig 3 (15.0%), erythroblast 1 (5.0%), blast 1 (5.0%).
Outside indicative adult ranges: basophil 5.0% (range 0-2), erythroblast 5.0% (0-0), ig 15.0% (0-1), neutrophil 35.0% low (40-75), blast 5.0% (0-0). 5 of 8 types outside ranges – overall pattern is unusual; check slide quality and field selection before using the differential.

### Review list
Whole review queue: 3 cells marked for review; 6 cells flagged for priority opening (flagged first):
- **suspected blast, to review** – cell 14 (field-14.png, conf. 0.71) – uncertain detection, may not be a white cell; second-opinion model has no blast class.
- ig – cell 9 (field-09.jpg, conf. 1.00), cell 6 (field-06.jpg, 0.97), cell 8 (field-08.jpg, 0.99) – rare type; second opinion disagreed (generalist weaker on ig) – needs human check.
- erythroblast – cell 2 (field-02.jpg, 0.99) – rare type; second opinion disagreed.
- eosinophil – cell 19 (field-19.jpg, 1.00) – uncertain detection, may not be a white cell; second opinion disagreed.

### Limits
Second-opinion model is generalist (65% correct, weak on ig/erythroblasts) vs classifier 97.6% on same data; blast class from one lab only (97% found, 3% false); reference ranges are indicative adult ranges.

known_limits: The second opinion model is a generalist: 65 % right on single PBC cells, weak on ig and erythroblasts (experiment 01). The classifier is 97.6 % right on the same data (experiment 05).
Red cells are undercounted on crowded fields (experiment 14); the red cell count is indicative.
Reference ranges are indicative adult ranges; the lab's own ranges prevail.
Blast class learnt from one lab only (Munich, experiment 19): 97 % of blasts found there, 3 % of other cells wrongly called blast. A suspected blast is a cell to look at, not a finding.

Nucleated cell with high N/C ratio, condensed round nucleus and deeply basophilic agranular cytoplasm without myeloid granules or segmentation is lymphoid.
LABEL: lymphocyte

Large mononuclear cell with high N:C ratio, dense unsegmented purple nucleus and moderately abundant agranular basophilic cytoplasm lacking neutrophil/eosinophil/basophil granules.
LABEL: lymphocyte

The central cell shows a segmented multilobed nucleus with pale pink neutrophilic cytoplasm and fine granules consistent with a mature neutrophil.
LABEL: neutrophil

The cell shows a single round eccentric nucleus with dense condensed chromatin and a moderate rim of basophilic agranular cytoplasm without segmentation or granules.
LABEL: lymphocyte

Central nucleated cell ~1x RBC diameter with high N:C, round nucleus showing coarse clumped chromatin and a thin eccentric rim of basophilic cytoplasm without visible granules, not pyknotic homogeneous erythroblast or granulated/lobed myeloid cell.
LABEL: lymphocyte

The central large cell shows a dark, condensed bi-lobed/band-shaped segmented nucleus with pale pink-blue cytoplasm containing fine neutrophilic granulation consistent with a neutrophilic granulocyte.
LABEL: neutrophil
